item.title: Region IV cross country roundup: New Braunfels girls sweep 5A titles
item.description: Members of Smithson Valley, New Braunfels and Boerne Champion girls cross country team stand on the awards podium after the Region IV-5A meet held Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026 at Texas A&M-Corus Christi. New Braunfels finished first followed by Smithson Valley and Champion. (Courtesy/New Braunfels Cross Country) New Braunfels, led by senior Savanah Moya, endured sloppy conditions to win the Class 5A Region IV girls cross country team championship by 46 points on Tuesday at Texas A&M-Corpus Christi. The Unicorns tallied 46 points, while Smithson Valley was second (88) and Boerne Champion third (97). Moya was the top individual performer, clocking 18 minutes, 56.96 seconds on the 5,000-meter course. Freshmen teammates Halle Bryant was third, and Tessa Shamblin was sixth. The Region IV championships were held Monday and Tuesday. The top four teams and top 10 individuals not on a state-qualifying team advance to the UIL state championships scheduled for Nov. 6-7 at Old Settlers Park in Round Rock. Boerne Champion senior Shawn Edwards won the boys 5A individual championship in 16:30.10 for 5,000 meters. He led the Chargers' second place team finish with 103 points. Weslaco East won with 98. Reigning Class 3A boys state champion Lytle claimed the regional title with 46 points, 37 ahead of second place Cole. Lytle sophomore Jacob Cantu was second (17:26.08) and junior teammate Adrian Reyna was fourth. Marion senior Jayce Love, who competed for Clemens last year, was the 3A boys winner (17:07.05). Randolph junior Caroline Finley won the 3A girls race in 13:01.86 over 3,200 meters. On Monday, New Braunfels Canyon won the 6A girls championship on a dry course. The Cougarettes (95) edged Churchill by three points. Churchill was led by a 1-2 finish by junior Kallie Van Pooyen (18:15.20) and sophomore Mia Kellogg (18:24.17). Top finisher for Canyon was senior Madison Molinar (18:40.74). Clark junior Calvin Pomeroy finished second in the boys 6A race in 15:19.04. Clemens was second in the team division with 143 points, 36 behind Round Rock. Sotomayor was fourth, making the first time the Wildcats qualify for state. Floresville junior Kaden Cypert earned his first regional championship by winning the 4A race in 15:36.41. He led the Tigers' second place finish, nine behind Great Hearts Northern Oaks' 129. Davenport's girls won the 4A team title with 93 points. The Wolves were led by freshman Raelin Cortinas' 19th place finish. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Jerry Jeudy as a man-coverage winner or Calvin Ridley as a veteran would at least be something. KC Concepcion reminds me of Zay Flowers Concepcion had a career-best game in Week 7 in terms of fantasy points (19.2 HPPR), expected points (15.2), targets (10), receptions (8) and yards (129). KC Concepcion YAC YAC YAC look at the hidden yards he picks up on final contact. Frequently an extra 5 yards, dragging the DB who ultimately brings him down pic.twitter.com/ElzKuNv7Cg — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) October 26, 2026 As my good pal Josh Norris notes, Concepcion will add the extra couple of yards by fighting on contact. Almost every clip from above shows that. Concepcion did drop an explosive Cover 2 hole shot and couldn't stack a fairly slow CB on a go ball, but those are volatile plays and Concepcion's underneath role is good enough to ride as an upside WR4. He's the WR41 on WR36 usage this month and is my favorite to lead the Browns in receptions and yards down the stretch. We'll see if he gets used in the red zone, however. The good news is he ran a route on all four dropbacks outside of 11-personnel last week. He's not a traditional slot. Through three quarters, snaps were Coleman (15), Dobbins (13) and RJ Harvey (12). If Dobbins doesn't run well early, he'll lose the veteran nod in a battle for the hot hand. Without any late-down snaps last week and minimal receiving work to fall back on, Dobbins can't be started in fantasy, even if the Broncos are running the ball more with Sean Payton back on the sticks. He is not an above-average athlete or powerful rusher, and he did overthink some runs, in my opinion. That said, he did find some hidden yards, too. It was a passable but not a needle-moving performance. I'd be surprised if Coleman “Wally-Pipps” Dobbins off this outing. It'll likely take some time, barring injury. item.title: Stoke City legend Dobing dies aged 87
item.description: Peter Dobing won eight caps for England at Under-23 level [Shutterstock] Stoke City legend and League Cup winner Peter Dobing has died at the age of 87. Manchester-born Dobing is best remembered in the Potteries as Stoke's skipper when they lifted the trophy by beating Chelsea at Wembley in 1972. Dobing, who began his career at Blackburn Rovers, made 377 appearances and scored 95 goals for the Potters after being signed by manager Tony Waddington from Manchester City for a then club record £37,500 in 1963. He had already made one previous appearance at Wembley, for Blackburn in 1960, when he scored five times in their run to the FA Cup final, only to lose 3-0 to Wolves. But his second chance to be a winner at the home of football, still a comparatively rare achievement for any player back then, came approaching the end of his career - and this time he took it. Dobing scored three goals in the 1971-72 League Cup, the most important of them in the semi-final second replay against West Ham United as the Potters went through 3-2 to reach Wembley and their first major final - and it ended in triumph as goals by Terry Conroy and George Eastham gave them victory. In a statement, the club said: "The thoughts and sincere condolences are with Peter's friends and family at this immensely difficult time. "With this coming Saturday being the club's Remembrance fixture, details regarding plans for a tribute to Peter on a forthcoming match day will be shared with supporters in due course." Watched by team-mates Jimmy Greenhoff, Gordon Banks, Harry Burrows and Jackie Marsh, Peter Dobing holds aloft the League Cup on the Potters' open-top bus parade back in Stoke after their famous win over Chelsea [Shutterstock] Dobing's father had played rugby league for Salford, but Peter opted for football, playing as an amateur for both Blackburn and Manchester United before signing a professional contract for Johnny Carey at Rovers in December 1955. He scored 20 league goals as Rovers gained promotion to Division One in 1957-58, including four in one match against Bristol City. He then hit a season's best 24 league goals in 1958-59, before Blackburn's run to the cup final in 1960 - and he then moved to Manchester City, also for £37,500, a year later when Denis Law left to join Italian side Torino. He was City's top scorer with 22 goals but when they were relegated a year later, Dobing moved on to newly promoted Stoke. In his first season at the club, he scored 19 goals as they reached the League Cup final for the first time, then held over two legs, which they lost to Leicester City. He broke his leg in January 1965 and was eventually moved back into a midfield role, where he played as Stoke won at Wembley in 1972. Dobing's second leg fracture proved a career-ending injury and he went on to work as a real life potter in the Potteries. Latest Stoke City news, analysis and fan views

item.title: Mainz humbled by second-tier Bochum in German Cup
item.description: Bochum's Philipp Hofmann celebrates scoring his side's second goal during the German DFB Cup 2nd round soccer match between Bochum and Mainz 05 at Vonovia Ruhrstadion. (is associated with: «Mainz humbled by second-tier Bochum in German Cup») David Inderlied/dpa Second-division Bochum caused a minor shock by knocking out top-flight Mainz in the German Cup second round on Tuesday. Danish forward Christian Rasmussen scored just after the break and Philipp Hofmann sealed the 2-0 home victory on 75 minutes. Mainz have been eliminated before the round of 16 for the fourth time in a row. RB Leipzig's roller-coaster season took another turn with a 2-1 comeback win at third-tier Rot-Weiss Essen having been reduced to 10 men in the first half. Lucas Brumme put Essen ahead after 9 minutes following a short back-pass from Castello Lukeba and a slip from Leipzig goalkeeper Ørjan Nyland. The night got worse for the Bundesliga side and under pressure coach Martín Demichelis when Nicolas Seiwald was sent off just before half-time for a second booking. Leipzig sacked boss Ole Werner in the close season despite finishing third in the Bundesliga and replacement Demichelis has a mixed record so far. But substitute Christoph Baumgartner, injured for much of the season, netted a double in the second period to send Leipzig into the third round. Third-tier hosts Sonnenhof Grossaspach fought back from 2-0 down to draw level but Bundesliga team Augsburg eventually prevailed 4-2. Eintracht Frankfurt triumphed 3-1 at fellow top-flight side Hamburg. Four games follow later on Tuesday including Borussia Dortmund against Werder Bremen. Holders Bayern Munich welcome second-tier Magdeburg in Wednesday's second-round matches.

item.title: Monster Energy Yamaha Star Racing Signs Casey Cochran For 2027
item.description: Ex-Husqvarna rider to compete in 250 class Photos by Yamaha and Husqvarna. Casey Cochran has his factory ride locked in for 2027. Monster Energy Yamaha Star Racing announced a multi-year deal that puts the 20-year-old from Portsmouth, Virginia, on the team's 250 program aboard the all-new YZ250F for the upcoming SuperMotocross World Championship season. The signing closes out what had been an uncertain stretch for Cochran. He had been under the KTM Group umbrella through GasGas and Husqvarna since 2021, but lost his seat for 2027 once Rockstar Energy Husqvarna confirmed its withdrawal from the series this past May. "I'm super stoked and grateful to be joining Monster Energy Yamaha Star Racing for the 2027 SMX season," said Cochran, who races the #49. "This is an opportunity I've worked hard for, and I'm ready to make the most of it. I can't wait to get to work with the team and see what we can accomplish together." Cochran is a six-time Loretta Lynn's AMA Amateur National Motocross Champion, and capped his amateur career in 2023 by taking the 250SX Futures Championship and AMA Youth Rider of the Year honors. His pro debut came that same year at the Budds Creek National. The pro ranks have given Cochran a tougher go. Injuries have dogged him every year since his AMA Pro Motocross debut in 2023, limiting his chances to show the pace that made him a standout amateur. He has racked up a fair number of Pro Motocross starts and scored an overall podium at the 2024 Spring Creek National, but enters 2027 with only four 250SX starts to his name. Whether he can stay healthy long enough to convert that amateur speed into results on the YZ250F is the open question hanging over the move. Cochran rounds out a six-rider Monster Energy Yamaha lineup alongside reigning 250SX East and 250MX Champion Cole Davies, plus Kayden Minear, Caden Dudney, Landen Gordon, and Pierce Brown. "He has impressed me for years, and I am looking forward to seeing what he can do on our team," said 250 team manager Jensen Hendler. "With our program, Casey's talent and his strong work ethic, I feel we have a winning combination." The 2027 season opens January 9 with the first round of Monster Energy AMA Supercross at Angel Stadium in Anaheim, California. Become a Motorcycle.com insider. item.title: ESPN analyst shares George Pickens trade idea that makes no sense for Cowboys
item.description: ESPN analyst shares George Pickens trade idea that makes no sense for Cowboys originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys just beat the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football with a dominant 38-21 victory. Dak Prescott and the Cowboys are now 3- 4 and have a chance to make the playoffs. While it's going to take Dallas making up some ground, the New York Giants are banged up and sitting at just 4-2-1. It's very possible to make up that ground to secure the NFC East division lead. The trade deadline might be a key time to make such a run. However, ESPN's Ben Solak shared a horrible trade idea for the Cowboys, one that would send George Pickens to the Kansas City Chiefs in a move that'd admit their odds of contending in 2026 are over way too early. Cowboys get horrible trade idea that sends George Pickens to Chiefs "Send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 conditional fifth-round pick to the Cowboys for George Pickens," Solak proposed. This trade idea would be a horrible idea for the Cowboys. While Solak is proposing this trade from the Chiefs' perspective amid the team's big wide receiver need, from the Cowboys' side of this deal, it would be a horrible mistake. Pickens has an uncertain future with the Cowboys, so if they lose Week 8 and Week 9, then maybe a trade could be justified. But if they win even one of those games, Pickens shouldn't go anywhere. They already bought Joey Porter Jr. in a trade, investing in the 2026 season. Trading Pickens, especially for such a lackluster return, wouldn't make sense for the Cowboys. But with Pickens involved, the Dallas offense is a really difficult one to stop, especially if Javonte Williams and the ground game get going as they did in Week 7. A Pickens trade would make sense in a lost season, since he's hitting free agency after this season. But with the Cowboys in contention for the NFC East and potentially finding their stride, Pickens getting traded would not make much sense. Solak's trade idea would be great for the Chiefs, but horrible for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb is great and the unquestioned No. 1. Ryan Fournoy is a solid No. 3 option as well. But with Pickens involved, the Dallas offense is a really difficult one to stop, especially if Javonte Williams and the ground game get going as they did in Week 7. A Pickens trade would make sense in a lost season, since he's hitting free agency after this season. But with the Cowboys in contention for the NFC East and potentially finding their stride, Pickens getting traded would not make much sense. Solak's trade idea would be great for the Chiefs, but horrible for the Cowboys. With games against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts before the deadline, the Cowboys should be 5-4 and clear buyers, not sellers, as Solak's trade idea implies. Liga match – began threatening along the right-hand side. In the 21st minute, SG94 midfielder Marius Kunde struck the post with a distance effort. A capacity crowd of 10,000 at the WIRmachenDRUCK Arena waited with bated breath whilst a lengthy VAR review checked for a possible offside position. Match official Patrick Schwengers officially confirmed the 1-2 in the 24th minute, sending the locals and their ultra section into convulsions. End-to-end action reigns for the rest of the half Sufficiently loosened up by the three goals, both teams showed little aversion to risk over the course of the rest of the opening half. The crowd found itself treated to some very entertaining football in which the ball swung from end to end. A clear-cut scoring opportunity may not have emerged for a while, but the optical quality of the football ensured that few spent much time sitting passively in their seats. Großaspach fullbacks Molinari and Rahn pressed exceedingly high, each generating half chances of their own. Shortly before the end of the first 45, the hosts came close to equalizing twice. FCA keeper Finn Dahmen had to remain on his toes to parry a deflected effort in the 45th. One minute later, SG striker Pollex nearly bungled the ball over the line. Before it was time to head into the locker rooms, Augsburg’s Young-Woo Seol forced an excellent save out of keeper Reule at 45+2. The hosts were gradually working their way into the game. One had the sense that the second half had something special in store. The equalizer comes! A corner two minutes after the restart enabled the underdogs to equalize. At first, nothing appeared to come of the 47th-minute dead ball. Lively SG94 fullback Luca Molinari was nevertheless able to get a second cross in. Großaspach skipper Volkan Celiktas rose highest to head the 2-2 home. The Bundesliga club, visibly rattled, struggled to mount a response. The hosts appeared content to allow the ball to circulate through the FCA ranks, but Baum’s charges couldn’t punch through with anything coherent. Baum’s substitutes swing the match The hour mark came and went with nothing to show for the Augsburg efforts beyond a couple of blocked shots. The Bundesliga trainer opted to freshen things up with the introduction of Arijon Ibrahimovic and Anton Kade in the 65th minute. Within ten minutes, both FCA subs got their names on the scoresheet. Juma Bah and Behrens were able to get a poorly fisted corner away to Ibrahimovic in the 70th. The Bayern Munich loanee finished from about 25 meters out with a curling effort into the right corner. Four minutes after that, it was once again Behrens supplying the assist for Kade. The 74th-minute 4-2 came from close range after a short counter the leggy hosts simply weren’t able to cope with. From that point forward, it was the Bundesliga side that looked more likely to score. Keeper Reule denied Fellhauer a chance at the 5-2 in the 83rd. The hosts were able to put together a pair of decent attacking sorties before the full-time whistle blew, but the guests never truly relinquished control of the game. He also won 63 percent of his 19 duels and prevailed in all four of his aerial challenges. His attacking contributions included two shots, three assists, and three chances created. Behrens’ development has been followed closely by Get German Football News since his summer arrival in Augsburg. The former TSG Hoffenheim prospect impressed during a loan spell with Heidenheim last season before joining Manuel Baum’s squad in search of regular Bundesliga football. As noted in GGFN’s comprehensive Augsburg season preview , Behrens’ versatility, athleticism, and ability to provide attacking impetus from deeper positions appeared ideally suited to Baum’s plans. His performance in Aspach provided another encouraging demonstration of those qualities. Several Großaspach players also deserve honorable mentions. Luca Molinari (8) was among the most impressive players on the pitch, scoring the hosts’ first-half goal. Elias Rahn (7), Volkan Celiktas (7), Marius Kunde (7), and Niklas Pollex (7) also earned considerable credit for their contributions against Bundesliga opposition. Kunde came particularly close to making an impact on the scoresheet when he struck the post from distance, while Pollex supplied the assist for Molinari’s goal. item.title: Football Daily | Harry Kane completes his arc from Orient loanee to Ballon d’Or winner
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Perusing the records we could find of Leyton Orient’s 4-0 shellacking of Sheffield Wednesday on a cold January afternoon in 2011 at Brisbane Road, Football Daily could find little or no indication that the young tyro who scored the O’s second goal might one day be presented with the most prestigious individual gong in world football. On loan from Spurs, a whey-faced 17-year-old Harry Kane marked his first senior start with what the BBC described as “a neat finish”, stealing in at the far post to convert a Dean Cox free-kick. Even after a breakthrough 2014-15 season for Spurs that yielded 31 goals and earned him an England call-up, assorted experts predicted Harry would prove to be little more than a one-season wonder – a kind of footballing Chumbawamba but with better manners and neater hair. Eleven seasons later the immensely likable Bayern Munich striker continues to bang them in for club and country with such monotonous regularity that few were surprised to see him presented with the Ballon d’Or ! Ballon d’Or!! Ballon d’Or!!! Ballon d’Or!!!! by the original and best Ronaldo live at the London Palladium. Not since the late Bruce Forsyth has any Englishman in an over-sized crushed velvet bow tie looked more at home on the famous old venue’s stage. Re: yesterday’s Football Daily . OK, so it may not be that contemporary, but Omar Berrada’s name fits into a jaunty song I came up with when bored, to the tune of Escape (the Piña Colada song) by Rupert Holmes: ‘If your name’s Omar Berrada / Head should be hangin’ in shame / If you’re supportin’ the Glazers / You’ve only got half a brain / If Jason Wilcox hasn’t done one / When he is mostly to blame / Then we’re the fans that you’ve stuffed / How do we stop the pain?’ I’m not even a United fan, but they’re all welcome – Simon Mazie. I would happily take the Manchester United job, as it’s a surefire way to earn three years’ pay in six months – Alex Lester. Now the shambles at United is even clearer, might Bryan Mbeumo be wishing he had chosen Spurs instead? – Richard Fernandez. About Jonathan Chester-le-Street’s excellent idea to nominate Noble Francis for the Fifa presidency ( yesterday’s Football Daily letters ). I back that nomination and look forward to his first act in office: the creation of a Noble prize, awarded to himself obviously – Peter Oh. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
